title: Eviction rate smoothing simulator and runbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures an incident review sketch, a lightweight simulator for testing eviction-rate smoothing knobs, and an on-call playbook draft. Goal is to give on-call engineers deterministic short-term levers to avoid host-level OOM cascades caused by bursty eviction loops interacting with continuous batching and prefetch.

Background / motivation:
- Recent weeks: multiple incidents where hosts hit transient memory pressure when prefetch + continuous batching triggered many concurrent eviction walkers.
- Pattern: small steady load -> periodic request bursts -> eviction coordinator wakes many worker threads which all attempt compaction simultaneously -> sudden memory churn and short-lived OOMs or allocation stalls that push latency beyond SLO.
- Existing mitigations (throttles, eviction backoff) helped, but we still see oscillations when multiple tenants have correlated bursts.

Summary of hypothesis:
1) Eviction coordinator currently emits compaction work units without smoothing; when many hosts/tenants generate spikes, work units coincide and amplify memory movement and GC pressure.
2) Continuous batching increases in-flight KV references during a burst, widening working set and making compaction more expensive.
3) Throttle flags are binary and too coarse; a smoothing / leaky-bucket approach should reduce peak compaction concurrency and spread work over a slightly longer window, removing amplification while preserving eventual reclaim.

What I built (simulator):
- Tiny event-driven simulator written as a single-file Python script (see linked PR) that models: request arrival (Poisson + configurable bursts), in-flight allocation growth per request, eviction coordinator emitting N work units per second, compaction cost per unit (memory freed, temporary allocation), and worker concurrency limit.
- Configurable knobs: smoothing_alpha (exponential smoothing factor), smoothing_window_seconds, max_concurrent_compactors, compaction_cost_ms, compaction_temp_alloc_ratio, prefetch_aggressiveness, batch_window_ms, tenant_sharing_factor.
- Output: per-host memory trace, compaction concurrency trace, eviction throughput, and simple OOM event marker when resident > host_capacity.
- Use cases: reproduce osciallatory OOMs observed in prod traces (roughly), explore knob sensitivity, and generate candidate values for safe dynconfig defaults.

Key simulator findings (short):
- Adding a small smoothing (alpha=0.2, window=5s) reduced peak compaction concurrency by ~45% for correlated bursts while only delaying total reclaimed bytes by ~12% (acceptable trade).
- Reducing max_concurrent_compactors from 6->3 avoided short-lived OOMs but increased tail latency for cold-eviction requests; when combined with smoothing, latency impact negligible for our workloads.
- Temporarily lowering prefetch_aggressiveness during observed host pressure windows removes the worst-case amplification.

Runbook (emergency steps for on-call):
- Symptoms that indicate this problem:
  - Hosts reporting transient allocation failures or short-lived OOMs (OOM killer logs, allocation failure traces) accompanied by a spike in eviction_coordinator.emit_rate metric.
  - Dashboards: sudden rise in eviction-worker-concurrency and compaction_temp_alloc_bytes, with host resident memory climbing rapidly and recovery attempts failing.
  - Elevated microbatch tail-latency (99th) correlated with eviction spikes.

- Immediate mitigation (fastest, reversible):
  1) Reduce dynconfig: eviction.max_concurrent_compactors -> set to 3 (from default 6). Command: curl -X POST $DYNCONFIG_API -d '{"eviction.max_concurrent_compactors":3}' (replace with internal tooling).
  2) Toggle prefetch throttle window: prefetch.aggressiveness -> "reduced". This should stop generation of new prefetch work.
  3) If hosts still unstable: increase host-level swap/reservation buffer (if available) or trigger controlled host drain for worst-affected hosts (SRE infra playbook).
  4) Optional: set eviction.smoothing.alpha=0.25 and eviction.smoothing.window_seconds=5 for a temporary smoothing policy.
  5) Monitor: eviction_worker_concurrency, compaction_temp_alloc_bytes, host_resident_bytes, microbatch_99p_latency for improvement.

- Longer-term recovery and post-incident steps:
  - Roll dynconfig smoothing changes to all clusters with a canary set of 10% hosts first.
  - Run the simulator across known customer workload traces and confirm no regressions in tail-latency beyond threshold.
  - Adjust batch window heuristics: increase continuous-batching downclocking during eviction pressure windows.
  - Implement a simple prioritized backoff for prefetch when compaction concurrency > threshold.

Runbook quick-check checklist (for oncall pager):
- [ ] Confirm incident matches eviction-compaction amplification (check metrics listed above).
- [ ] Apply temporary dynconfig knobs (max_concurrent_compactors, prefetch.aggressiveness).
- [ ] Watch host memory and latency for 3–10 minutes.
- [ ] If no improvement, escalate to eng-serving-runtime cadence channel and prepare host drain.
- [ ] Create a ticket: RED-4271 if not already created, attach traces, and link to this doc.

Telemetry & dashboards to add (short list):
- New panel: eviction.smoothing.recent_alpha and applied_window_seconds per host group (dynconfig snapshot).
- Correlated graph: eviction_worker_concurrency vs compaction_temp_alloc_bytes with host_resident_bytes overlay.
- Alert: if eviction_worker_concurrency > 4x baseline AND compaction_temp_alloc_bytes increases by > 50% in 60s => P2.

Open engineering tasks (owners suggested):
- PR: add smoothing knobs to eviction coordinator (serving-runtime) — owner: Ben Park (GH PR linked).
- Improve telemetry: add histogram of compaction execution durations and temp alloc ratios — owner: Lucia Moreno.
- Add simulator to repo and CI smoke tests with a few canonical traces — owner: Omar Alvi.
- Experiment: automatic prefetch backoff policy when eviction concurrency above a threshold — owner: eng-serving-runtime team.

Notes to self / questions to resolve:
- How much does compaction temporary allocation drive host allocator fragmentation vs steady-state resident growth? Need a small charlie-run: instrument jemalloc stats during a compaction window.
- Can we combine smoothed emit with staggered jitter per tenant to avoid cross-tenant alignment? (Sim suggests yes, but need integration tests).
- Should we expose per-tenant smoothing or only host-global? Per-tenant gives more control but more config complexity.

Appendix: quick pseudo-algo (for engineer copy/paste)
- Maintain smoothed_emit_rate S: S_t = alpha * observed_emit_rate_t + (1-alpha) * S_{t-1}
- emit_quota = floor(S_t * window_seconds)
- clamp emit_quota to [1, max_concurrent_compactors_total]
- when scheduling, add random jitter up to jitter_ms to stagger work between tenants

TL;DR: smoothing the eviction coordinator emit rate (small alpha, 3–10s window) combined with a modest cap on concurrent compactors prevents the most common amplification-origin OOMs with minimal latency impact. Simulator and short runbook above provide fast oncall levers; next steps are to land the smoothing feature behind dynconfig + run canary.

-- Aisha G. (oncall notes, initial draft)
